## Status

GREEN locally, review ready at `32582421bbf095a7b5a7d4b953c4d737b86fe54b` — `696-maap-annexb` -> `dev`.

Round 7 answers R558-7 and R559-6 at `d1b18b3f` with four commits on top of it (no rebase, no amend).
It changes the MAAP harnesses, the planted-defect campaign and the documentation only: no RTL, record or route change.
The unit suite now establishes the recorded first-draw criterion for every seed from the RTL itself.
It names each first-draw check for what it grades, and it reads the DEFEND's requested start for a PROBE that starts below this station's offset.
At the round-7 head the MAAP suite passes 186 unit checks and 5 real-datapath checks.
Its campaign catches 63/63 planted defects and passes both controls.
Those defects include R559-6's q3 and q9, R559-6's q1 (R558-7's q3) and R558-7's overlap-start echo.
Coverage is 225/225 lines, and the documentation and static set passes.
The MAAP differential (12/12 cases, 17/17 defects), lint (90 <= 90) and 404 behaviour scenarios pass at the head.
The hosted sweep shard that owns the MAAP suite (`--shard 1/5`) passes 23/23 suites (196,929 checks) at the head, with its four declared field-campaign skips.
The round-6 evidence for the unchanged RTL and suites stands.
The parent sweep passed 61/61 suites (2,185,927 checks) at `30242308`, and portability passed 58/58 tops there.
The firmware bank (471/471 defects caught) and the pinned field campaigns (AAF 164, gPTP 677) passed at `d1b18b3f`.

All three resource endpoints, measured through the recipe at `bee1b0d7`, pass the gate and are re-recorded:
`route-1x1` LUT 50,013 (-217), FF 54,306 (-2), slice 15,753 (-70), storage and DSP unchanged, WNS +0.233 ns, WHS +0.017 ns, fully routed;
`ooc-1x1` and `ooc-8x8` keep every recorded figure. The MAAP block measures 490 LUT / 340 FF, +51 / +60 against the base, within its ceiling.

## Description

The fabric MAAP allocator (`KL_maap`) closes the Annex B deviations left after #686:

| Item | Clause | Change | Check and planted defect |
|---|---|---|---|
| M4 | B.3.4 NOTE; B.3.6.1 | Seed sampled from the programmed MAC at first enable, not at reset. The first Begin! draws its offset and its first probe interval from the generator one step past that seed, through parity folds of all 32 bits | Real-datapath checks: two MACs draw different intervals, and two fixed pairs claim disjoint first blocks and different first offsets. Unit checks over equally timed stations (sampled pairs 2^i apart, R558-6's fixed pairs) and, for every seed, the recorded criterion through first-draw maps learned from the RTL. `m4_reset_time_sampling`, R558-6's p7 (unit and datapath), the raw-seed first offset, the fold without the high half, the raw-seed first probe draw, R559-6's q3, q9 and q1, a nonlinear first fold and a probe row repeating an offset row are caught |
| M2 | B.3.6.6 | DEFEND echoes the PROBE's requested start and all sixteen count bits | Named checks for the requested start (also for a PROBE starting below this station's offset) and for the count; three defects caught |
| M7 | B.4; Table B.9 | A supplied range outside the dynamic pool is refused (bounded draw instead) | Boundary checks; two defects caught |
| M8 | B.2 | Truncated PDUs are discarded with no state, timer or TX effect; counting withdrawn by ruling | Cycle-matched comparison with idle RX; two defects caught |
| M1 | Table B.7 note d; B.3.6.4 | MAC comparison in the rProbe!/PROBE and rDefend!/DEFEND cells | Both cells; two defects caught |
| M5 | B.3.5.9; Tables B.3 and B.7 | Rising link revokes and re-probes; a falling link is no event; wired from the existing effective link | Unit checks for a return and for an outage longer than a walk, and a real-datapath check; four defects caught |
| M6 | Table B.7; B.3.6.6 | One shared buffer keeps a DEFEND pending while PROBE or ANNOUNCE drains | Four named checks; five defects caught; one-response capacity documented |
| M3 | B.3.6.1 | 32-bit generator, period 2^32 - 1, seeded at first enable from MAC plus the existing PHC; continues across Release/Begin | Eight defects caught, two through the real datapath (one of them a first offset that ignores the clock); pool-fold bias documented |

The firmware differential programs 1,024 MAC identities before first enable and keeps every timing bound and both draw assertions.
A MAC-ignoring parent now draws 5,230..5,801 cycles and fails the draw-coverage check at its low end (at most 5,200).

### Review rounds

| 6 | R558-6 NEGATIVE at `6de3904e` | R558-6-F1 (below); R558-6-R1: this body's head and this table | `30242308`, `05eca371`, `bee1b0d7`, `b7f342ae`, `d1b18b3f` |
| 7 | R558-7, R559-6 NEGATIVE at `d1b18b3f` | R558-7-F1, R559-6-F1, R559-6-F2 (below); residues R558-7-R1 and R559-6-R1 | `8e8f0343`, `4a54d852`, `49c0a83c`, `32582421` |

### Review round 7 (R558-7-F1, R559-6-F1, R559-6-F2)

The RTL is unchanged. This round changes the MAAP harnesses, the campaign and the documentation.
The separation criterion is the one recorded in assignment 6102832618, which narrows round 6's.
Two seeds a power of two apart, with any carry run, claim disjoint first blocks of up to 8 addresses through the pool fold and the clip.
Seed bits 16..31 map one-to-one onto the offset word. Other pairs carry no separation guarantee beyond B.3.6.1's random draw.

- **Check names (R559-6-F1).** Each first-draw check is named for what it grades.
  Section [12] grades disjoint first blocks for "adjacent MACs", "MACs 2^i apart (16 <= i <= 31)" and "MACs 2^i apart (1 <= i <= 15)".
  It grades different first offsets for "clocks 2^k apart" and different first probe intervals for "MACs 2^i apart".
  R558-6's four MAC pairs and two clock pairs have their own checks, named as fixed pairs.
  The two datapath first-claim checks name their pairs as fixed pairs too, and the campaign anchors follow every rename.
- **Every seed (R559-6-F2).** A new section [13] learns the first offset word and the first probe draw as linear maps of the seed.
  It learns them from the RTL's own first Begin!: reset, program the MAC, enable, then read the claimed offset and the first PROBE's timer load.
  It confirms both maps on 256 further seeds. It then claims every word of the offset image through the RTL for block sizes 1 to 8 (524,288 claims).
  Five named checks follow. The maps must be linear in the seed.
  All 528 carry runs, against every word and size, must claim disjoint first blocks and draw different first probe intervals.
  Seed bits 16..31 must map one-to-one onto the offset word, and the two first draws must be independent.
  No fold row, generator tap or pool bound is restated in the harness, so a changed constant is graded as it stands. The section adds about one second.
- **Plants.** R559-6's q3 (offset row 0, `32'h0000_0081` to `32'h0000_0080`) fails only the one-to-one check.
  Its q9 (row 6, `32'h8008_0040` to `32'h8000_0040`) fails only the every-run disjointness check; both pass every sampled pair.
  Its q1 (the probe fold of the unstepped state; R558-7-S1 and R559-6-S1) fails only the every-run probe check.
  A nonlinear first fold fails the linearity check, and a probe row repeating an offset row fails the independence check.
- **M2 echo (R558-7-F1).** At `[4b]`, the only fixture whose PROBE starts below this station's offset, a named check reads the DEFEND's requested start.
  The plant `m2_echo_overlap_start` echoes `conf_start_w` and fails that check alone.
- **Residues.** R558-7-R1's and R559-6-R1's exact texts are applied to `MAAP_FABRIC.md`, and R559-6-R1's to this body.
- **Reviewer probes, at the head.** R558-7's `reviewer_probes.py`: q1 CAUGHT at the new M2 check, q3 CAUGHT; q4 (R558-7-S2) still escapes; the other seven CAUGHT.
  R559-6's `probes.py`: q1 and q3 CAUGHT; q5 (R559-6-S3) and q8 (R559-6-S2) still escape; the other four CAUGHT. Its `q9_probe.sh` reports 186 checks, 1 failure.

### Review round 6 (R558-6-F1)

At `6de3904e` the first Begin! offset was the raw low 16 bits of MAC + clock, and the first probe timer read the raw seed's low 6 bits.
Equally timed stations whose MACs differed only in bits 16..31 claimed the identical first block; adjacent MACs claimed overlapping ones.
R558-6's p7 (the pre-#696 first draw) passed every check.

- **RTL (`30242308`).** The generator, its period and the M3 seed load are unchanged.
  The first Begin! offset is now `rand_offset(offset_fold(lfsr_step(seed)))`: the generator one step past the seed, as the firmware core steps before its first draw.
  Each offset bit is the parity of the stepped seed under one row of `OFFSET_FOLD_C` (16 rows, at most three stepped bits each).
  Every probe interval is `518 + probe_fold(next state)` ms; at the first PROBE the next state is the same stepped seed (`PROBE_FOLD_C`, 6 rows).
  No flip-flop is added.
- **What the folds guarantee.** For two seeds 2^i apart, with any carry, the offset words keep blocks of up to 8 addresses disjoint through the pool fold and the clip, and the first probe draws differ.
  That covers adjacent MACs, MACs one power of two apart and, at one MAC, clocks one power of two apart.
  Seed bits 16..31 map one-to-one onto the offset word, so MACs differing only in bits 16..31 always draw different words; the pool fold can still map two such words onto one block, so their first blocks can coincide or overlap like any pair that is not a power of two apart.
  The 22 rows are independent, so the first offset and first probe interval are jointly uniform.
  Pairs that are not a power of two apart can still overlap at the rate of two independent draws (about 15 in 65,024); no 16-bit draw can separate every pair.
- **Checks (`30242308`).** Five unit checks in section [12] over stations reset and enabled on the same cycles: 33 adjacent-MAC pairs (every carry length), 139 pairs differing only in bits 16..31, 360 pairs 2^i apart, 34 clock pairs and 52 first-interval pairs, R558-6's four pairs among them.
  Round 7 splits these: 136 of the 139 are 2^i apart (16 <= i <= 31), and R558-6's pairs and two clock pairs are now checks of their own, named as fixed pairs.
  Two datapath checks read the first PROBE's requested range on the real CSR path: adjacent MACs claim 0x7029 / 0x9821, and two PHC times claim 0xf229 / 0xf1cd.
  The campaign adds R558-6's p7 (unit and datapath), the `6de3904e` raw-seed first offset, a fold without the seed's high half, a first offset that ignores the clock (unit and datapath) and the raw-seed first probe draw; each fails its named check.
- **Reviewer probes.** R558-6's `first_draw_probe.cpp`, unchanged, now prints `disjoint` for all four pairs (0x0109/0x4901, 0x0109/0x4109, 0x7a78/0x3ef8, 0x8174/0xa044) with different first intervals.
  Its `reviewer_probes.py` with only the p7 anchor re-pointed to the new first-draw text reports p7 CAUGHT in both harnesses; unchanged, it reports that anchor missing.
  p6 still escapes (R558-6-S1, optional, not in this round).
- **Differential (`bee1b0d7`).** The MAC-ignoring plant now fails the draw-coverage check at its low end rather than its high end, so the driver accepts either end of that check (the two assertions sharing the words "MAC/phase sampling reaches the parent's").
- **Docs (`05eca371`).** `MAAP_FABRIC.md` and `KL_maap.md` describe the first draw, the folds and the guarantee exactly.
- **Area and records (`b7f342ae`, `d1b18b3f`).** The MAAP block grows by 45 LUTs and no flip-flop, to 490 / 340, within the +60 / +60 ceiling.
  Each endpoint's measured inputs differ from the preceding record's only in `KL_maap.sv`; the standalone wrapper does not instantiate it, so both standalone endpoints are unchanged.
  The route passes every gate (floor, fall limit, tolerances, primitives, routing) with no exception, and all three records are re-written by `record --write` with unchanged policy.

## How to get into the same state

```sh
git fetch origin
git checkout 696-maap-annexb
git rev-parse HEAD   # 32582421bbf095a7b5a7d4b953c4d737b86fe54b
git submodule update --init third_party/verilog-axis protocol-processor gptp-processor third_party/lwSRP
: "${WORK:?Set an empty disk-backed scratch directory}"
: "${VERILATOR:?Select the pinned 5.050 executable}"
: "${MILAN_RV32_CC:?Select the verified RV32 compiler}"
export TMPDIR="$WORK" VERILATOR VERILATOR_JOBS=2 MILAN_RV32_CC
```

Use the pinned documentation environment and matching coverage reader.
Set `FIELD_GENERATOR` to the clean tsn-gen revision pinned by `.github/workflows/rtl.yml`, with its packet generator built.

## How to validate

```sh
make -j8 -C tb/verilator/maap MDIR="$WORK/unit"
make -j8 -C tb/verilator/maap integration-build DP_MDIR="$WORK/integration" && (cd "$WORK/integration" && ./maap_integration)
make -j8 -C tb/verilator/maap coverage COV_MDIR="$WORK/coverage"
python3 sw/firmware/ctrl/test/maap_differential.py --self-test --keep "$WORK/differential"
python3 sw/firmware/ctrl/test/test_ctrl_firmware.py --require-rv32 --self-test --jobs 2
bash scripts/run_all_suites.sh "$WORK/parent-suite-logs"
TSN_GEN_ROOT="$FIELD_GENERATOR" make -j8 -C tb/verilator/tsn_fuzz
bash syn/yosys/run.sh --results "$WORK/portability-results"
python3 scripts/lint_rtl.py --check --self-test --jobs 2
(cd tests && behave --no-capture -f plain)
python3 scripts/xvlog_gate.py --check
python3 scripts/docs_check.py
python3 scripts/gen_toc.py --check
python3 scripts/check_em_dash.py --base "$(git merge-base origin/dev HEAD)"
python3 scripts/measure_test_evidence.py --check
python3 syn/ooc/pp_resource_gate.py check-baseline
```

The first command builds and runs the unit harness, then the planted-defect campaign.
To see R558-6's p7 fail on its own, build the unit harness against a copy of `KL_maap.sv` whose first draw is the pre-#696 expression:

```sh
python3 -c 'import sys; s=open(sys.argv[1]).read(); a="rand_offset(rng_seeded_r ? lfsr_next_w[15:0]\n" + " "*68 + ": offset_fold(seed_next_w), count_i)"; assert s.count(a)==1; open(sys.argv[2],"w").write(s.replace(a,"rand_offset(lfsr_next_w[15:0], count_i)"))' \
    hdl/ieee1722/maap/KL_maap.sv "$WORK/KL_maap_p7.sv"
make -j8 -C tb/verilator/maap run MDIR="$WORK/p7" MAAP_RTL="$WORK/KL_maap_p7.sv"   # fails by design
```

Measure the three endpoints with the [baseline recipe](docs/testing/PP_SHADOW_BASELINE_RECIPE.md), `--single-thread-synthesis`,
and `--integrated-clock` for both standalone runs, with no other heavy job beside Vivado. Then:

```sh
python3 syn/ooc/pp_resource_gate.py check "$ROUTE" --endpoint route-1x1
python3 syn/ooc/pp_resource_gate.py check "$OOC_1X1" --endpoint ooc-1x1
python3 syn/ooc/pp_resource_gate.py check "$OOC_8X8" --endpoint ooc-8x8
```

Expected result / pass criteria: every command in the first and last blocks exits 0.
- The MAAP suite reports 186 checks and the datapath 5 checks, all with 0 failures.
- The campaign reports 65 rows: 63 defects exit 1 at their named check, and the two clean controls exit 0.
- The p7 copy reports 186 checks and 9 failures. Six are first-claim checks: adjacent MACs, MACs 2^i apart (16 <= i <= 31), MACs 2^i apart (1 <= i <= 15), R558-6's fixed MAC pairs, clocks 2^k apart and the fixed clock pairs.
  The other three are the every-seed disjointness, one-to-one and independence checks.
- Coverage is 225/225 lines. The differential passes 12/12 cases and catches 17/17 defects.
- The parent sweep reports 61/61 suites, and its four field-campaign skips are covered by the separate `tsn_fuzz` run.
- Each endpoint check prints `RESULT: PASS` against the committed records.
- The field campaign rewrites only the timestamp line of its two generated result pages; discard that change.

## Known limitations / out of scope

- M6 stores one pending or transmitting response. Further PROBEs while occupied remain unsupported, including during DEFEND.
  Full Table B.7 conformance is not claimed. B.3.6.6 defines the response action; B.3.6.3 defines probe-count decrement.
- M3 corrects period and seeding; the pool mapping (fold and clip of the 16-bit draw) remains biased under B.3.6.1.
- The first-draw separation is guaranteed for seeds a power of two apart and blocks of up to 8 addresses (the criterion recorded in 6102832618). Other pairs can overlap at the rate of independent draws.
  Only the first Begin! after reset uses the folds for its offset; later Begin! and Restart! draws read the running generator, as before.
- No check grades that later Begin! events read the running generator (R558-7-S2, R559-6-S3).
  No check drives a random draw into the pool clip with a block size other than 8 (R559-6-S2, older than #696).
  Both are optional suggestions outside this round, and their probes still escape.
- M8 counting needs a register-map change and was withdrawn by ruling; truncated PDUs are discarded without effect.
- Tagged MAAP reception remains outside this correction lane.
- The MAAP FF allowance (+60) is fully used; round 6 adds no flip-flop.
- Acceptance 4 (bench interop with the reference peer) belongs to the post-merge bench lane.
- The full parent sweep and portability last ran at `30242308`, the firmware bank and field campaigns at `d1b18b3f`.
  Round 7 changes only the MAAP suite's harnesses and campaign and two documentation pages; the MAAP target, datapath, coverage, differential, lint and behaviour ran at the head.
  The processor banks were not rerun: pins and processor sources are unchanged.
- Hosted checks and the local workflow replica need the pushed head.

## Composition repair

The composition review [R558-9](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/706#issuecomment-6113540239) found that, once merged with dev, the Mark II plan's M2 and M6 sections called the 50,267-LUT route "the `route-1x1` record", which this PR re-records at 50,013. `a7291311` merges dev `09c7231e`. `aa980479` makes `docs/design/MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md:695`, `:696` and `:947` name #645/#647's record (the gate record at dev `e8454e27`) and state that both lanes also pass against this PR's record. `:706` and `:968` now say each lane does not re-record the gate (R558-9-R1). `docs_check.py`, `check_em_dash.py --base 09c7231e`, `gen_toc.py --check` and `--verify-anchors`, `check_doc_paths.py`, `check_doc_style.py` and `syn/ooc/pp_resource_gate.py check-baseline` pass at `aa980479`.
